subject: [Action Required] Bluehaven — WebSocket chunk timeouts causing elevated latency/errors
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya@bluehaven.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Realtime API — intermittent websocket hangs since 06/01 morning

Hi Karthik,

We started seeing elevated request latency and a small but growing number of WebSocket timeouts on our prod cluster this morning (around 08:30 PST). Users report long pauses during live document summarization sessions — the UI shows the spinner for 20–40s before the stream resumes or fails. Error rate went from ~0.3% to ~2.8% over the last 2 hours, and throughput dropped ~15%.

Attached is a small sample of client-side traces and the JS console logs. We pushed a quick rollback to an earlier client version but the problem persisted, which makes us think it’s server-side. This is affecting an active campaign and we’re starting to get negative customer feedback.

Can you triage and let us know if this is on your side or if we need to pause traffic?

Thanks,
Maya
Customer Success — Bluehaven

Attachments: bluehaven-client-trace-0601.json (4 KB)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya@bluehaven.ai>
Cc: sergio.alvarez@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 01 Jun 2028 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Realtime API — intermittent websocket hangs since 06/01 morning

Maya — thanks for the quick heads up and the traces. I’m looping in Sergio (SRE) and Neha (Customer Ops).

Initial read: the client traces show long gaps in token delivery consistent with chunk timeouts on our WebSocket frontends. I’m starting a capture on the Bluehaven routing pool and will share logs. Can you confirm approximate affected model (gpt-3.5-redwood-live or gpt-4-redwood-lowlatency) and whether these sessions used streaming with chunk_size override?

Short ask: Please hold off on pausing traffic for now — we’ll attempt a soft-fallback to a compatible model variant and continue captures. If the error rate crosses 5% we’ll recommend a maintenance window.

Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Maya Patel <maya@bluehaven.ai>
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 01 Jun 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Realtime API — intermittent websocket hangs since 06/01 morning

Maya/Karthik — I pulled the websocket front-end and proxy logs for Bluehaven’s routing pool (pool-us-west-2-bluehaven). Findings so far:

- Between 08:20–09:00 PST we see an intermittent spike of 503s from the internal chunk-assembler service — correlated with an increase in per-connection inflight queues.
- There are repeated "chunk timeout" errors where the chunk-assembler did not receive a continuation frame within 15s for ~1.9% of streams.
- Downstream inference nodes are healthy (GPU metrics normal); KV cache hit rate unchanged.

I’m attaching the raw sampler and a targeted trace bundle. Next steps I’m executing now:
- Increase websocket keepalive frequency for this pool (from 60s to 20s) for 30m as a mitigation.
- Temporarily reduce max-concurrent-streams-per-connection limit to reduce head-of-line blocking.
- Start a canary fallback route to the 16-bit quantized model variant for long sessions to see if chunk durations normalize.

I’ll report back in 45–60m with telemetry. If error rate keeps rising we should escalate to execs for a customer SLA exception.

Attachments: bluehaven-ws-samples-0601.log.zip (2.8 MB)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Jun 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Realtime API — intermittent websocket hangs since 06/01 morning

Evelyn — forwarding an active Bluehaven incident. Sergio’s already running mitigations but error rate is creeping up and Bluehaven is a strategic expansion account (deal BH-EXP-2028-09). Need executive visibility in case we need credits or an SLA exception; customer is seeing production impact and is escalation-ready.

Summary: chunk assembly timeouts on websocket pool causing 15–25s pauses for some long-running streaming sessions; current mitigation: keepalive frequency increase + connection concurrency throttle + model fallback canary. Early telemetry shows a small improvement but not resolved.

Proposed immediate ask for leadership: if the error rate exceeds 4% or customer requests compensation, approve an up-to-$25k service credit and a 24-hour dedicated SRE rotation. Also recommend a 30-minute exec sync with Bluehaven to set expectations if we fail to fully restore within 2 hours.

I’ll attach the incident plan after Sergio finalizes the mitigation steps.

—Karthik

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 03 Jun 2028 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Bluehaven incident update — mitigation applied and next steps

Maya/Tom — quick update following our interventions:

What we observed: intermittent chunk assembly timeouts on your websocket routing pool caused sporadic 15–30s pauses for long streaming sessions and a temporary bump in error rate.

What we did: increased websocket keepalive frequency, reduced per-connection concurrency limits for a targeted window, and ran a canary routing to the quantized model variant for affected sessions. We also captured a bundle of traces and logs (attached).

Outcome: since the mitigations the error rate has decreased from a peak of ~2.8% down to ~0.9%. Throughput has recovered to within 97% of baseline. We will keep the interim throttles in place for another 12 hours while we complete a root cause analysis.

Next steps:
- Sergio and our infra team will run a deeper post-incident RCA focused on chunk assembly backpressure and proxy-to-assembler queuing.
- We will provide an RCA document and telemetry summary by EOD Monday and a remediation timeline for a permanent fix (kernel/runtime tuning for the chunk assembler).
- If you prefer, we can schedule the 30-minute exec sync tomorrow to walk leadership through the RCA and remediation plan.

We’ve attached the trace bundle and a short mitigation plan. If you notice anything else or want the exec sync, reply with times that work for you.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0182
